case_name: Jaswinder Singh vs State Of Punjab & Another

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Punjab & another, respondent No.2 (wife)

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing FIR No.25 dated 9.2.2009, under Sections 323,406,498-A & 506 IPC. Parties have arrived at a compromise and respondent No.2 has received Rs.7 lacs as full and final maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: The High Court has the power to quash prosecution where it feels that the same is required to prevent abuse of process or secure ends of justice.
legal_principles.held: As per the Full Bench judgment of this Court in Kulwinder Singh and others vs. State of Punjab, 2007 (3) RCR (Criminal) 1052, High Court has power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to allow the compounding of non-compoundable offence and quash the prosecution where the High Court felt that the same was required to prevent the abuse of the process of any Court or to otherwise secure the ends of justice.
cited_cases: Kulwinder Singh and others vs. State of Punjab, (2007) RCR (Criminal) 1052
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent abuse of process

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash criminal proceedings lies with the court and should be exercised when it is required to secure ends of justice.
legal_principles.held: The question which is required to be answered in this case is whether the power which independently lies with this Court to quash the criminal proceedings pursuant to the compromise arrived at, should at all be exercised?
cited_cases: Nikhil Merchant vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another JT 2008 (9) SC 192
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to secure ends of justice
